tasks.name: The Morning Route
tasks.text: On Monday morning Ollie and Mum leave home early. They walk to the bus stop near the park. The bus number seven arrives in three minutes. Mum pays for two tickets, and they sit near the window. The streets are busy: cars, cyclists and a big yellow van. At the third stop a crowd of schoolchildren gets on. Ollie gives his seat to an old lady. She smiles and says: Thank you, young man! At the metro station they get off and go down the stairs. The train is already waiting.

tasks.name: The Metro Map
tasks.text: At home Jack shows Ollie a map of the metro. Every line has its own colour and number. The red line goes through the centre, and the blue line goes to the stadium. To get to the museum, you need to change trains at Park Station. Ollie traces the route with his finger. It looks like a colourful spider web! Jack says: Read the signs above the platform and follow the arrows. If you get lost, ask a station worker. Tomorrow the boys will travel alone for the first time. Ollie is a little nervous but excited.

tasks.name: A New Bike Lane
tasks.text: A new bike lane opens along the river. Sophie and Lily ride there after art school. The lane is wide and bright green. A sign says: Cyclists only. Sophie rings her bell and laughs. They pass an old bridge, a small café and a row of trees. Near the park Lily stops suddenly: Look, a little cat! The kitten sits between the bikes and looks scared. Sophie picks it up carefully and reads the address on its collar. The girls take the kitten home, and its owner is very happy. What a useful bike lane!

tasks.name: At the Bus Stop
tasks.text: Mrs. Green waits for the bus with two heavy bags. The bus is late, and it starts to rain. Ollie runs out with an umbrella and helps her carry the bags to the shelter. They sit down on a dry bench. Mrs. Green tells him about the old trams that used to run here many years ago. She remembers the conductor, the wooden seats and the bell. Ollie listens with interest. When the bus finally arrives, they get on together. At the next stop Mrs. Green says: Thank you, dear. You made a rainy day much warmer!

tasks.name: Dad’s Shortcut
tasks.text: On Friday David drives the children to school. The main road is full of cars, so he chooses a shortcut through small streets. First they pass a bakery, then a garage and a tiny square with a fountain. Ollie watches the house numbers and gives directions. Turn left here! Now go straight! At one corner a delivery van blocks the way. David laughs: So much for my shortcut! They turn around and take another street. In the end they arrive just in time. Next time, says Sophie, we will take the metro!

tasks.name: Where Is the Museum?
tasks.text: The Carters want to visit the city museum. Near the park they meet Ollie and ask: Excuse me, could you tell us the way to the museum? Ollie smiles: Of course! Go straight along this street, then turn right at the traffic lights. The museum is on the left, opposite a big bookshop. Mrs. Carter repeats the route to remember it. Mr. Carter says: Your English is very good! Ollie laughs: I practise with George every day. The family walks together to the corner. Before saying goodbye, George gives Ollie a small map of London.

tasks.name: The Lost Phone
tasks.text: George cannot find his phone. He looks in his pockets, under the bench and in his school bag. Nothing! Ollie says: Don't worry. Let's ask the people in the park. They approach a young woman with a pram. Excuse me, have you seen a black phone? No, sorry. Then they ask a man walking his dog. He points to the fountain: I saw something black near the water. The boys run there and find the phone on a low stone wall. George is relieved: Thank you! My parents' numbers are inside. Next time I will keep it in my jacket.

tasks.name: Across the Bridge
tasks.text: Mrs. Carter needs a pharmacy. The nearest one is across the river. Ollie draws a simple map on a piece of paper: first the bridge, then the square, then the second corner. They walk together and talk about the city. Mrs. Carter says that in Sydney the streets are wider and the river is much bigger. Ollie answers that he has never seen the sea. Really? she asks. Then you must visit us one day! At the pharmacy she buys medicine for Emily, who has a bad cold. On the way back they stop for hot chocolate.

tasks.name: A Polite Question
tasks.text: Mr. Carter gives Ollie a short lesson in polite questions. Excuse me, could you tell me where the bank is? he asks slowly. Ollie repeats the phrase. Good! Now ask the way to the theatre. Could you tell me how to get to the theatre? Excellent! Mr. Carter explains: In English, polite questions sound longer, but people answer them more gladly. Ollie practises with George at the door. Excuse me, could you tell me where my football boots are? George laughs and points under the sofa. Even at home, polite words work!

tasks.name: The Right Bus
tasks.text: Emily wants to visit her friend, but she is afraid of taking the wrong bus. Ollie looks at the route map with her. Number seven goes to the library, number twelve to the swimming pool, and number twenty-three to the shopping centre. You need number twelve, he says. Get off after the bridge, at Green Street. Emily repeats the stop name three times. At the bus stop Ollie says: Remember, ask the driver if you are not sure. Emily smiles: Thank you for your help!

tasks.name: Tickets to Grandma’s
tasks.text: On Saturday the family goes to the old railway station. The building has a tall clock tower and big glass doors. Dad buys tickets at the window: four returns to the village. The cashier says: The train leaves from platform three at ten fifteen. Don't be late! Ollie reads the departure board. He finds their train between two fast trains to the capital. Mum checks the bags: pie, warm sweaters and a book for Grandma. At the platform a loud voice announces: The train to the village is ready.

tasks.name: The Clock Tower
tasks.text: Aunt Sarah is waiting under the clock tower. She has just returned from a long trip and carries a bright yellow suitcase. You are just in time! she says. Look at the station clock — it is ten minutes slow. They laugh and walk to the platform together. Sarah gives the children small presents: postcards from three countries and a box of sweets. Ollie asks: Aunt Sarah, how many languages do you speak? She answers: Two well, and three badly! Then she shows them the words she learned on the plane. Everyone tries to repeat them.

tasks.name: On the Train
tasks.text: The train moves slowly through the city, then faster between green fields. Ollie sits by the window and counts small stations, cows and red roofs. A conductor comes to check the tickets. He smiles at the children and says: The next stop is yours. Mum opens the bag with the pie, and the whole carriage smells of apples and cinnamon. Sarah tells a story about a night train in Italy. Outside, the rain begins, and drops run across the glass like little trains. In forty minutes they will see Grandma on the platform.

tasks.name: Grandma’s Garden
tasks.text: Grandma Margaret waits at the gate of her small house. The garden is full of apple trees, red flowers and buzzing bees. Grandpa George is in his workshop, repairing an old radio. He comes out with oil on his hands and hugs everyone. Lunch is already on the table: soup, fresh bread and the famous apple pie. After lunch Ollie helps Grandma pick apples. Sophie draws the garden, and Jack tries to fix the garden gate. The cat sleeps in a wheelbarrow.

tasks.name: The Last Train Home
tasks.text: Time passes quickly. After dinner Grandpa looks at his watch and says: The last train leaves in thirty minutes! Everyone hurries to the car. The road is dark, and the headlights light up the trees. At the station they run to the platform just as the train appears. Grandma waves from the gate. Goodbye! Come again soon! Inside the carriage Ollie falls asleep on Mum's shoulder. Sophie holds the jar of apple jam. The train carries them home through the quiet night. At the door Dad whispers: A perfect day. Everyone agrees.

tasks.name: The Museum
tasks.text: On Sunday the family visits the city museum. The building looks like a huge palace with columns and tall windows. In the first hall there are dinosaur bones. Ollie reads the sign: This dinosaur lived millions of years ago. Wow! In the next room Sophie finds paintings of old streets and ships. Jack studies a model of the first bridge. Suddenly the lights go out for a moment. Everyone laughs nervously. The guard explains: It is part of the show. When the lights return, a huge whale hangs above their heads.

tasks.name: Lunch at the Café
tasks.text: After the museum everyone is hungry. They choose a small café near the river. The waiter brings the menus and asks: Are you ready to order? Dad takes the soup, Mum a salad with cheese, and the children want pasta. Ollie cannot decide between pizza and pancakes. The waiter smiles: Why not both? First pizza, then pancakes for dessert. Everyone laughs. While they wait, they watch boats on the river. The food arrives hot and smells wonderful. At the end Dad asks for the bill.

tasks.name: The City Park
tasks.text: After lunch the family walks to the city park. There is a big pond with ducks and small boats. Ollie wants to row, and Jack agrees to help. They take a blue boat for half an hour. Sophie sits on the shore and draws the bridge. Mum and Dad drink coffee on a bench. A street musician plays the violin under a tree. George and Emily join them with a bag of bread for the ducks. The ducks are not shy at all! When the boat returns, Ollie has wet sleeves and a happy face. This is the best part of the day, he says.

tasks.name: The Rainy Plan
tasks.text: Suddenly the sky turns grey and big drops fall on the park. The family hides under a tree, but the rain becomes stronger. Dad says: New plan! We are going to the cinema. They run to the bus stop and reach the old cinema just before the film starts. The film is about a brave dog who travels across the country. Ollie hugs Buddy in his imagination. When they come out, the streets shine with rain. The city looks different: bright signs, umbrellas and puddles like little mirrors. Maybe the rain was a good idea after all.

tasks.name: Home by Metro
tasks.text: In the evening the family goes home by metro. The station is warm and full of light. Trains come and go, and people hurry in every direction. Ollie counts the stops: one, two, three... At the fourth stop they change lines. A musician plays the guitar on the platform, and a little girl dances with her mother. Sophie smiles: The metro is like a city under the city. At their station they climb the stairs. The rain has stopped, and the air smells fresh. Home is near. Ollie yawns and says: Today was a real adventure.
